anti_overlap: Does not evaluate protocol conformance language or version contract mechanics — see fd-protocol-conformance
Does not evaluate prose clarity or naming vocabulary — see fd-doctrine-clarity and fd-naming-vocabulary-discipline
Does not evaluate ecosystem layering or plugin architecture patterns — see fd-ecosystem-layering
decision_lens: For every addition: would this behavior need to change if the host were Claude Code or a custom CLI instead of Hermes? If no, it belongs upstream. If yes, is the Hermes-specific reason documented?
focus: Upstream/adapter ownership boundaries — what legitimately lives in the adapter vs. what drifts upstream or duplicates it
name: fd-adapter-boundary-rigor
persona: Apply the perspective of a distributed systems boundary architect — they care about clean ownership demarcation between host-specific and protocol-canonical layers, measure whether each added behavior has a host-specific justification, and flag any behavior that would be equally valid for non-Hermes hosts as misplaced in the adapter.
review_areas: Each category of Athenflux additions (orchestration policy, prompt packaging, artifact lifecycle, operator workflow, runtime integration) has a crisp host-specific justification that cannot be satisfied by parameterizing interflux
The qualification rule (documented workflow, stable convention, explicit artifact semantics, documented boundary) is testable — not aspirational prose
The 'what Athenflux should not own' list is complete and each item has a clear reason it remains upstream
No behavior added by Athenflux is a renamed copy of existing interflux behavior without documented divergence rationale
The boundary rule ('if it matters equally in Claude Code, it belongs in interflux') is applied consistently across all proposed additions

severity_examples.condition: The adapter re-implements selection logic that interflux already owns, creating a fork risk and a future sync burden
severity_examples.scenario: Athenflux redefines review-mode routing without referencing interflux's existing domain detection and staging logic

severity_examples.condition: Duplicate definitions will diverge under independent maintenance; one must be canonical and the other must reference it
severity_examples.scenario: The promotion ladder (Draft → Reviewed → Candidate canonical → Canonical) is defined identically in both the adapter spec and interflux docs with no cross-link

severity_examples.condition: Behavior that is host-agnostic should live upstream; the adapter spec should contain only the Hermes-specific subset
severity_examples.scenario: Handoff conventions (when to save a skill, open an issue, update README) are framed as Hermes-specific but contain no Hermes-dependent condition

success_hints: Every addition in §'Added by Athenflux' survives the 'would Claude Code need this too?' test with a documented answer
The qualification rule is phrased as observable conditions, not capability claims
Cross-links to interflux canonicals are present wherever the adapter inherits without modification
task_context: Review the Athenflux adapter spec to evaluate whether each proposed addition is correctly scoped to the Hermes host layer and whether the upstream/adapter boundary is rigorously drawn throughout the document.
